Bulgarian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed through French archéologue or German Archäologe, in turn from Byzantine Greek ἀρχαιολόγος (arkhaiológos), from ἀρχαῖος (arkhaîos, “primal, old, ancient”) + λόγος (lógos, “speech, oration, study”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɐrxɛoˈɫɔk]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian, l-vocalization):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔk
  • Syllabification(key): ар‧хе‧о‧лог
  • Hyphenation(key): ар‧хе‧олог

Noun

[edit]

археоло́г • (arheológ) m (feminine археоло́жка)

  1. male archeologist

Alternative scripts
Arabic ارحەولوگ
Cyrillic археолог

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian архео́лог (arxeólog), from ἀρχαῖος (arkhaîos, “primal, old, ancient”) + λόγος (lógos, “speech, oration, study”).

Noun

[edit]

археолог • (arxeolog)

  1. archaeologist

Ukrainian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Possibly borrowed from German Archäologe. Also analyzable as архео(ло́гія) (arxeo(lóhija)) +‎ -лог (-loh). Compare Russian архео́лог (arxeólog), Belarusian архео́лаг (arxjeólah), Polish archeolog.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɐrxeˈɔɫɔɦ]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

архео́лог • (arxeóloh) m pers (genitive архео́лога, nominative plural архео́логи, genitive plural архео́логів)

  1. archaeologist
